newsitem.title: USA: Green Tree says $3/EPS in 1997 achievable.
newsitem.headline: Green Tree says $3/EPS in 1997 achievable.

text.p: Green Tree Financial Corp chairman and chief executive officer Lawrence Coss backed analysts earnings estimates for 1997 of about $3.00 a share.
"The consensus is around $3.00 (EPS in 1997)," Coss told Reuters following the company's shareholder meeting. "We think that's an achievable number. We're comfortable with that."
First Call's mean estimate is $3.02 in 1997, a 37 percent increase over the $2.20 earned in 1996.
Coss also said he expects the financial services company to do $14 billion in loan volume this year - compared with the $10.56 billion in 1996 - and to seek acquisitions.

"We expect to produce finance volume that will exceed $14 billion this year, representing more than a 35 percent increase over last year," Coss said. "We will also consider opportunistic acquisitions, if the expected returns exceed our internal rates."
Coss said he expects the company's consumer finance unit to grow to $1.3 billion in loans in 1997, a 73 percent increase over $752 million in 1996.
"We think consumer finance loans will substantially exceed $1 billion this year," Coss said. "That business is growing very nicely. I think we'll see $1.3 billion."
